business_rules.statement: In-flight runs stay pinned regardless [SoW Fact — §3.8, §5.12.2]. No version change re-bases an in-flight run.
A Lane B decision is never auto-approved, and the publication that follows is automatic and fully audited [SoW Fact — §6.7.4, §8.4.4].
business_rules.enforcement_point: Client Command Center decision + auto-publish pipeline

business_rules.statement: The Statement of Work never describes unpublishing or rolling back a published version; prior versions are retained in full and remain permanently readable.
The republish description is mandatory at every republish; release is the Release Authority's, adoption is the Job Owner's.
The Author, Reviewer and Release Authority remain three distinct people; the severity floor cannot be weakened by any version.

A certification-requirement change applies to runs scheduled after the version carrying it is published, with active assignments grandfathered but flagged and the supervisor confirming continuation with a recorded reason.

At expiry under the strict posture, re-assignment to runs requiring the expired certification is blocked, the worker may complete the entire current run, and there is no grace period beyond it [SoW Fact — §4.4.4].

Archiving a Site or Area auto-pauses every bound Job, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list and prompts reassignment before archival completes; the cascade cannot silently strand a standing Job [SoW Fact — §4.3.3].
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift routes to the Quality Manager regardless of worker, because repeated exceptions in one Area are a signal about the Area.
Under hard suspension no new version may be adopted because that is a configuration change; a worker never clears their own block.
The qualification block is enforced on-device and is never dependent on a notification having been read.
Export-on-archival is provided at no charge [SoW Fact — §4.2.4]; archival and erasure execution are critical-class actions.
Legal hold is a managed object that suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its scope while in force, is dual-approved, tenant-visible and audited [SoW Fact — §8.17.3, §10.1].
Anonymisation is the lifecycle's one irreversible act, and switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later cannot resurrect identities already anonymised [SoW Fact — §8.17.4].
Nothing is purged anywhere on the platform: the tenant-set retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon, and beyond it data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable [SoW Fact — §10.1].
Every device wipe is preceded by a final sync attempt of pending captures; a device is not treated as wiped until it confirms.
Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the client identifies which standards those are [SoW Fact — §10.1].
Full traces are retained 24 months while the derived decision record persists for the full term of the operational record it explains [SoW Fact — §8.6.3, §10.4].

Tenants may make the platform stricter than default; they may never make it looser than the platform floor, and the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it [SoW Fact — §1.5].
An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, so a validation that passes but cannot be recorded must fail [SoW Fact — §4.10.1, §8.18].
Every validation failure resolves to exactly one of three postures: hard block, park, or flag-and-proceed. No silent posture exists.
No validation failure clears user-entered data on any of the five surfaces.
An action whose audit event cannot be written in the same transaction does not commit.
The pipeline stops at the first failing dimension and does not continue evaluating, so that no message can leak information from a later check the actor was never entitled to reach.
Every restriction is declared at six enforcement points, and a restriction is only real when the server point is present.
business_rules.enforcement_point: user interface, server, background processing, command delivery, synchronisation, audit

business_rules.statement: Every restriction in this blueprint declares a server enforcement point; a restriction with only a user-interface point fails release review.
Background processing re-evaluates restrictions at execution time, not at queue time.
A command that would violate a restriction never reaches the available-for-delivery state.
An upload that would violate a restriction is quarantined and surfaced, never silently accepted or silently discarded.
Consumption is never reset on a tier change: a tenant on Starter with 80 Worker-Shifts consumed that upgrades to Growth keeps the 80 against the new ceiling of 199 [SoW Fact — §4.2.2].

A downgrade whose target ceiling sits below current consumption does not fail and does not truncate; it queues, is labelled pending downgrade, and takes effect at the start of the first cycle in which consumption fits.
There is no payment integration anywhere on the platform, so no validation may depend on a payment event [SoW Fact — §4.2.1, §8.12].
A shift edit never alters the shift stamp of a completed run.
Cross-midnight runs take their production date from the shift's nominal date [SoW Fact — §2.4].
Self-attestation is not permitted; qualifications are entered by supervisors with a full audit trail, and the audit trail rather than a second approval is the control.
The expiry schedule is a four-stage alert at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days; tenants may add earlier warnings and may never remove or delay a stage [SoW Fact — §4.4.3].

Recertification's new expiry must postdate the previous expiry; back-dating the issue date is allowed, and both the certification date and the entry date are recorded so a late entry creates no apparent gap.
A Job cannot reach active without an approval by a different identity than its creator.
Removing the last approver-capable role holder is refused while any Job exists.
A run finishes on the workflow version it started on, in every case, including after a mid-shift publication.
A cancelled run preserves partial data and excludes it from the summary.
The only in-flight edits are worker substitution and end-time extension; the extension is supervisor-authorised, reason-required, capped at shift end plus a tenant-set maximum, and audited.
At least one severity mapping is required per measurement screen, so no measurement can be authored without a defined consequence for departing from its limits.
The locale-completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale, so a Spanish-reading worker can never be shown an English-only safety instruction.
No identity may complete two stages of the same submission.
No version change is applied inside an in-flight run on any device.
Evidence is immutable at creation; corrections are append-only annotation records carrying who, when, and what changed, and the original is never altered.
Captured media stays in the application's encrypted store and never touches the device gallery [SoW Fact — §7.8.4].
A capture that fails server validation is quarantined and surfaced, never discarded.
Conflicts resolve last-write-wins by device capture timestamp, guarded by the clock-skew threshold; a timestamp outside the threshold is not trusted to order writes and routes to human resolution.
Detection is deterministic and interpretation is agentic: no artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger [SoW Fact — §3.2].
The Severity 1 floor never moves: automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation, platform-fixed [SoW Fact — §3.3].
business_rules.enforcement_point: device + server, rejected at save if weakened

business_rules.statement: Where the freeze lands is determined, never chosen: the Lot where a lot exists, the Unit where work is serialized, otherwise the Run [SoW Fact — §3.3].
Hold state renders as issued, propagating, or in force per device, never as a single boolean.
Anomalies carry Open to Resolved with a closure note; a move to Resolved without a closure note is refused.
Channels are in-app and email only, platform-wide, at every tier, and in-app notifications cannot be muted [SoW Fact — §4.9.1, §8.14].
Escalation routing names recipient roles and never named individuals; a recipient specification naming an individual is rejected.
A routing rule with no resolvable recipient role is rejected at save, because the platform never lets an escalation resolve to no one [SoW Fact — §6.10.5].
Lane A self-tunes automatically, logged, reversible and tenant-visible, and by definition changes no configured value; Lane B never changes without a person.

The evaluation gate is hard for every tenant and binds every operator of the platform console including the root account: no agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios.
An undecided Lane B proposal is flagged stale at 30 days and never expires.
Emergency pause never suppresses on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
Maker-checker governs mutating administrative change: a Platform Engineer's change is submitted and takes effect only when an Admin approves it [SoW Fact — §8.8.3].
Root-only actions are user creation and role changes.
There are exactly three named platform access classes: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
The platform does not offer an approval bypass to any identity, including the root, because bypassing maker-checker is exactly the failure mode the control exists to prevent.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorisation, approval, suspension, or a device command.
Sending is not delivery; delivery is not opening; opening is not acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not the business action.
A server-created command does not mean an offline device received or applied it; command states are tracked separately and no surface may collapse them.
An event matching no notification category is refused and raised as a defect rather than delivered uncategorised.
Notification severity, deviation severity, and anomaly severity are stored in three separate fields and are never derived from one another.
Exactly two channels exist in the codebase; no third channel adapter ships in V1.
The Frontline inbox is unreachable from inside a run player step.
A notification is a pointer to a business object, never a carrier of authority; the click re-runs authorisation from scratch.
Email acknowledgement occurs only after an authenticated session exists, pending DEC-NOTIFACK-001.
All on-shift holders of the routed role at the Location are notified, and the first acknowledgement claims the item [SoW Fact — §6.10.5].
Routing resolution is on-shift only; there is no on-call calendar at V1.
Acknowledgement from any channel writes the same single state on the record.
An acknowledgement that cannot be written is never displayed as written.
No surface displays a notification as delivered to a device that has not synced since the notification was created.
A notification that cannot be audited is not sent.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen; the change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, and no code path exists where a change lands and its audit row does not.
business_rules.enforcement_point: transaction boundary; ENFORCED invariant locked with no off position for any account including the root

business_rules.statement: Tamper-evidence by chained hashes or signed batches is deferred beyond V1; V1 delivers append-only with no delete or edit path on any surface, an access-control property rather than a cryptographic one.
Nothing hidden means: no privileged exemption, no silent path, no acting-as-role fiction, and no one-sided visibility (cross-tenant access events mirror into the tenant's own stream).
No audit event class includes a password, token, key, or secret field.
Every event class has an explicit field allowlist enforced at build time.
Every mutating application programming interface path writes an audit event in the same transaction; a mutating path with no audit write fails the build.
Refusals are audited as a first-class class.
Reads are audited only where the source requires it, inside the three named platform access classes; general read auditing is deliberately not invented.
No audit event carries an acting-as-role claim; the log records the user identity and the action.

contradictions.description: §4.6.8 ties `complete` to the Execution Summary being computed while §6.2.6 ties it to every assigned device having synced; the two definitions can diverge for hours.

contradictions.description: §8.13.4 makes device enrollment tenant self-service while §7.5.2 assigns enrollment and lifecycle to the Super Admin console.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A published version carries a wrong severity band that is already in use on the floor
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Adopt the corrective version for every affected Job and rebase scheduled-not-started runs
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Runs are already in flight on the wrong version
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Those runs finish on the version they started; the records carry the version number as the audit receipt and affected units are dispositioned through the anomaly path
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The corrective version is published and adopted; audited-recompute and append-only corrections apply

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The 1-day qualification warning fails to deliver by email
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The unmutable in-app notification carries the same content
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nobody acknowledges within the two-minute window and no Supervisor holder is on shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Escalation falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback, and the certification still expires and the block still applies at step level on the device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recertification recorded on 24 August, block lifted over the command channel at next sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The export cannot complete because of its volume
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Export in scoped batches by date and entity, using the same filters the audit export offers
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The export still cannot complete before the commercial deadline
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Archival does not proceed; the tenant remains hard suspended, its data intact and its audit continuing
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The export completes and archival proceeds; archival re-approved by the root if the earlier approval has aged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tiering or anonymisation run fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-drive the occurrence from the durable queue, preserving the original due time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The re-drive fails repeatedly
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The data stays where it is; a failed tiering run leaves data in hot storage, a failed anonymisation leaves identities in place — neither failure can delete anything
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The run executes once the blocking condition clears, marked as a late execution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The validation pipeline cannot complete because a dependency it consults is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-evaluate once against the last-known-good cached copy, marking the decision as cache-based in the audit event
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No trustworthy cached copy exists; the platform must not guess a permissive answer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action is refused with "This action cannot be checked right now, so it has not been performed. Nothing has been changed."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on dependency health returning to healthy; cache-based decisions re-evaluated with divergences raised

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A dimension's authoritative configuration cannot be read
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Use the last-known-good value and mark decisions taken under it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No cached value exists, for example on a freshly enrolled device
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device refuses actions governed by that dimension: "This device is still setting up its safety rules. You can view your runs but cannot record results yet."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On first successful sync; decisions taken under cached values re-evaluated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The locale file for the actor's language is unavailable or incomplete for a message key
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Render the English default string, marking the render as a locale fallback
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The message key is absent from both locale files
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The surface renders the reason code and the generic string, never a blank dialogue and never a technical stack message
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The missing key raises a locale-completeness defect to the client's platform team

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The authority store cannot be read, so effective authority cannot be computed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Use the authority snapshot bound to the current session, valid for that session only, marking every decision taken under it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No session snapshot exists, for example at login
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform refuses to establish the session: "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. No work has been lost." — never granting a default authority of any kind
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic when the store returns; snapshot decisions re-evaluated and divergences raised

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A suspension state change is applied centrally but the command channel cannot deliver it to some devices
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains available for delivery and is applied at each device's next sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A device never returns
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant's central state is authoritative and every server-side action is refused; no surface may display that device as suspended
failures_fallbacks.recovery: At reconnection the device applies the pending suspension, locks with the fixed message, and preserves local data

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Site's time-zone data cannot be resolved, so a shift boundary cannot be computed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Use the last-known-good time-zone record and mark computed boundaries as provisional
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No cached record exists, for a newly created Site
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Site cannot be activated: "This site cannot be used until its time zone is confirmed." Escalation falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, visibly marked
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On time-zone resolution; provisional boundaries and Worker-Shift metering recomputed as an audited correction

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The qualification store is unreachable at gate evaluation on the server
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Evaluate against the work package's packaged qualification requirements and the device's cached qualification state, within the offline trust window
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The cached state is older than the trust window (default ~24 hours, 72-hour ceiling)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The gated step is blocked and the run parks; the platform never falls back to permitting a gated step on stale cache
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On sync; steps completed under cached qualification state re-evaluated on upload, divergences quarantined

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The automatic finish job cannot run at its due time
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The finish executes on the scheduler's recovery, computing from the original due time rather than the recovery time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The scheduler remains unavailable beyond the window's ceiling of 7 days
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Affected runs remain complete, marked "Closing delayed — platform operations notified", still accepting late captures flagged as late arrival
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Scheduler restoration triggers a backfill; every late finish writes an audit event naming original due time, actual finish time, and captures folded in

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A published version's package cannot be built or distributed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Devices continue on their currently pinned packages; the publication is marked published but not yet distributing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The package build fails permanently, for example because a referenced library asset is missing
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The version remains published with a distribution-blocked marker, no device receives a partial package: "Version 2.2.0 is published but has not reached any device. No run is affected."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rebuild after the referenced asset is restored; distribution state per device reconciled at each sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The durable local queue cannot accept a capture, most plausibly because device storage is exhausted
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device must refuse new capture rather than accept a capture it cannot durably hold
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The queue is corrupt rather than full
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The application enters a read-only, upload-only mode and blocks new capture: "This tablet cannot safely record new results. Your existing results are safe and are being sent. Use another tablet to continue."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: After successful drain of the queue and an integrity check; gaps raise a capture-loss investigation event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The release command cannot reach a device holding the frozen lot
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains available for delivery and applies at the device's next sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device does not return within the shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot remains held on that device: "Released centrally. 1 of 2 devices has not yet applied the release." No surface may state the lot is released while a device still holds it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On reconnection; propagation lag recorded as telemetry and unapplied release carried into the end-of-shift brief

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A routing rule resolves to no on-shift holder of the target role
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant has no Quality Manager available at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The escalation is recorded as undeliverable, rendered as "No recipient could be reached for this escalation", and raised to the Tenant Admin and platform operations; the underlying safety state is unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On a role holder becoming available, the escalation re-delivers and the gap is recorded rather than erased

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An agent cannot produce its output, for example the Shift Handoff Agent producing no brief
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surface states the absence plainly — no brief was produced for the named shift and platform operations has been notified
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The agent layer is unavailable platform-wide, or emergency pause is in force
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agents render as unavailable, never silent; in-flight agent runs checkpoint and park, raised gates stay human-decidable, and the on-device deterministic layer continues untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume is a separate audited act, never an automatic consequence of the pause condition clearing; stale-evidence proposals re-derived

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The approval service is unavailable, so no maker-checker cycle can complete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Changes remain in the submitted state and nothing applies: "Approvals are temporarily unavailable. Submitted changes are safe and will apply once approved."
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An urgent safety change is required while approvals remain unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform does not offer an approval bypass to any identity, including the root; the available action is the compliance-emergency path with its two authorisations
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On approval-service restoration the queue is processed in submission order; expired-precondition changes returned to their proposer

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The platform cannot determine a notification's true state, for example because provider feedback is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Hold the last confirmed state and mark the item as state unknown since a stated time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: State remains unknown past the acknowledgement timer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Treat the notification as unacknowledged, fire the escalation's fallback tier, and mark that fallback visibly, because assuming delivery is the unsafe direction
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On provider feedback returning; the audit trail retains both the assumed and the confirmed sequences

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A business event arrives that matches no notification category
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Route it to a platform-operations defect queue and deliver nothing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The defect queue itself is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The event is written to the audit log as an unroutable notification event, preserving the fact that something happened even though nobody was told
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The category is added through the normal change path; unroutable events replayed with original event time preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A category's severity assignment is missing
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Treat it as High, delivering immediately on both channels and requiring no acknowledgement
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The assignment table itself is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Deliver in-app only, at Standard priority, marked as unclassified, and raise a platform defect
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On ratification or table restoration; no re-delivery occurs because duplicate delivery of a safety item is its own hazard

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The email vendor is unavailable or rejecting
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery is unaffected and remains the primary channel; email retries under a bounded backoff schedule
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The vendor remains unavailable past the category's acknowledgement window
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The notification stands as delivered in-app and failed by email, both states visible; the escalation's fallback tier fires on the acknowledgement timer as normal; the platform does not invent a substitute channel
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on vendor restoration, with pending emails sent carrying their original event time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A category's rule card is incomplete at release
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The release gate blocks
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — a blocked release has no further degradation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The category does not ship, and its triggering event routes to the unroutable-event path of §30C.2
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Complete the card

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The pushed-event channel to open Command Center sessions fails, so the feed stops updating
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surface falls back to its refresh interval, default 60 seconds with a per-tenant floor of 30 seconds, and marks the feed as refreshed rather than live
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refresh also fails
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The board degrades gracefully to its last-synced picture with an age marker, and never goes blank
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On channel restoration, missed events are replayed in order retaining original origin and receipt times

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Revalidation cannot complete because the authorisation service is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None is permitted that opens the object
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: not applicable — no permitted fallback opens the object
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The click lands on an explanation screen: "This item cannot be opened right now because your access could not be confirmed. Nothing has been missed; the item is still in your list."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on service restoration; the notification remains in its pre-click state so no timer or escalation is affected

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The on-shift roster cannot be resolved
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resolve against all holders of the role at the required scope regardless of shift, marking every such delivery as an unverified-shift delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The role holder list itself is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The escalation is recorded as undeliverable and raised to the Tenant Admin and platform operations; the underlying hold or block remains in force independently
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On roster restoration; unverified-shift deliveries re-listed with the correct on-shift resolution and both retained in the audit

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The acknowledgement write fails, so a recipient believes they have acknowledged and the record does not agree
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surface refuses to show the acknowledged state until the write is confirmed, and retries the write once
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The write cannot be confirmed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The item stands as unacknowledged, the timer continues, and the recipient sees "Your acknowledgement has not been recorded. This item is still waiting."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on service restoration; duplicate acknowledgements recorded without re-claiming

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The preference store is unavailable when a notification is being routed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver on both channels and mark the delivery as preference-unavailable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant policy store is also unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Deliver in-app to all resolved role holders and suppress nothing, raising a platform incident
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on store restoration; preference-unavailable deliveries counted and reported to the Tenant Admin

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The device syncs but the inbox back-fill fails while command pull succeeds, or the reverse
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the failed half independently, because the two are separate flows and one must not block the other
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated failure of the back-fill
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device operates with commands applied and an inbox marked "Messages could not be updated. Your work instructions and permissions are current."
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic at the next sync; the server re-sends the difference and queued acknowledgements upload with both timestamps preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Email vendor unavailable; in-app delivery path unavailable; routing cannot resolve recipients; the notification service wholly unavailable; the audit store cannot record the notification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Email fails → in-app continues with bounded backoff retry; in-app fails → email continues and the in-app item is created on restoration with its original event time; routing cannot resolve → marked Quality Manager fallback; service wholly unavailable → notifications created from the event log on restoration
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both channels fail simultaneously, or the service fails and the event log cannot be replayed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Notifications recorded as undeliverable with their reason, Tenant Admin and platform operations raised, every safety mechanism remains in force, and no surface displays any notification as delivered; where the audit store cannot record a notification, the notification is not sent
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Replay in event order with original event times and duplicate suppression; RTO/RPO TBD under DEC-RTO-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A test in the notification test list cannot be executed because the behaviour it defends is not yet implemented
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The release gate blocks on the missing behaviour rather than on the missing test
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The behaviour is descoped
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The descope is recorded as an accepted risk with a named owner and a date, and the corresponding acceptance criterion is marked as not met in the release record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Implementation and re-test; the release record updated with the closure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An event class attempts to write a field outside its allowlist in production
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The write is refused and the action is refused with it, under the one-transaction rule
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The refusal itself cannot be recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action does not occur, the surface displays the audit-unavailable message from §30B.2, and a platform incident is raised through the monitoring path rather than through the audit path
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the event class and redeploy; no reconciliation required because nothing was written and nothing was changed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A new mutating path ships without an audit write, defeating coverage
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The build assertion prevents it; if bypassed, the runtime one-transaction wrapper refuses the write path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A path exists that neither the build nor the wrapper covers
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The path is disabled by feature control on discovery, and every change it made is reconstructed from the business record and written as a retrospective audit class explicitly marked as reconstructed, never as original
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Implement the audit write and re-enable; reconstructed events carry their reconstruction basis

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A required audit field cannot be resolved at write time, for example the actor's roles at the time
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resolve from the session snapshot, bound to the session and known at sign-in, marking the field as snapshot-derived
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No snapshot exists
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The event cannot be written completely, so the action is refused under the one-transaction rule
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On dependency restoration; no reconciliation required because nothing changed
